provenance.basis: Fictional reconstruction of a user-authorized manual author-critic workflow

careerFacts.text: Maintained an inherited municipal scheduling service and implemented reliability fixes. The candidate did not create the service.
Built an OpenAPI client generator integrated into build checks and wrote setup guides that other engineers used independently.
Compared persistence alternatives and presented a study. The proposed migration was not executed.
Owned a Python and PostgreSQL parcel-event ingestion feature with retries, idempotency, replay, deduplication, and partial-failure handling. The team released the product.
Introduced contract tests and quality checks retained by the team. Supported a production incident investigation and remediation, then added a regression test.
Collaborated remotely with distributed partners through written design notes and operational handovers.

Built BorrowDesk, a library-equipment lending prototype using cloud event queues and a merge queue that validated branch batches. It ran only in a demonstration environment, with no production users or independent scale measure.

Uses coding agents daily for design, implementation, tests, and infrastructure, and reviews changes personally and verifies tests before accepting them. Built DraftMate, an experiment alternating independent author and critic roles with evidence-linked decisions and human approval. This does not establish automated parity or enterprise AI governance.
Took technical-lead responsibility in a small team, including scoping, architecture, reviews, and mentoring. No Staff title or organisation-wide authority is established.
Completed a computing degree, a Distributed Application Design course, and a Cloud Operations workshop.

opportunity.title: Staff Platform Engineer
opportunity.description: Improve developer platforms, testing, build and merge workflows, and reliable backend services. The role also calls for cross-organisation technical direction, production cloud operations, and familiarity with the company's proprietary observability suite.

requirements.text: Own production backend services end to end.
Build developer tools, build checks, and merge workflows.
Use coding agents with engineering judgment and tested changes.
Communicate clearly in writing and work autonomously with remote partners.
Collaborate on technical direction across an organisation.
Use the company's proprietary observability suite hands on.

referenceCv.headline: Backend Engineer | Developer Platforms | Event Processing

statements.text: Backend and developer-tools engineer with production experience maintaining an inherited service and owning a team-released event-ingestion feature.

Built an OpenAPI client generator integrated into build checks and wrote setup guides used independently by other engineers.

Owned a Python and PostgreSQL parcel-event ingestion feature with retries, idempotency, replay, deduplication, and partial-failure handling; the product was released by the team.
Introduced contract tests and quality checks retained by the team; supported a production incident investigation and remediation, then added a regression test.
Wrote design notes and operational handovers while collaborating remotely with distributed partners.
Led technical work in a small team through scoping, architecture, reviews, and mentoring.

Built BorrowDesk, a library-equipment lending prototype with cloud event queues and branch-batch merge validation in a demonstration environment; it had no production users or independent scale measure.

Uses coding agents daily across design, implementation, tests, and infrastructure, reviewing changes personally; built DraftMate as an experiment in alternating independent author and critic roles with evidence-linked decisions and human approval.
Demonstrated Python and PostgreSQL ingestion, OpenAPI tooling integrated with build checks, team-retained contract tests, and branch-batch validation in a staging project.
Computing degree; Distributed Application Design course; Cloud Operations workshop.

coverage.rationale: The evidence supports ownership of a bounded production feature and related production reliability work; it does not justify generalising end-to-end ownership across the career.
Retries, idempotency, replay, deduplication, and partial-failure handling are stated for the owned production event-ingestion feature.
Production OpenAPI build tooling and team-retained checks support this requirement; branch-batch merge validation is adjacent prototype evidence only.
Daily coding-agent use with personal review and tested changes is stated, without a measured productivity claim.
Written design notes, operational handovers, and remote work with distributed partners are explicit.
Technical direction and mentoring are established within a small team; organisation-wide Staff authority is not.
Cloud event queues appear only in a staging demonstration prototype, with no production operation established.
No evidence of using the proprietary observability suite is supplied; keep this requirement as an explicit gap.
